advances: The fixed-table separator of `9fdba5fffd591cda` extends to a sharp symbolic height-strip inequality throughout the full-doubleton one-zero singleton chamber, including its \(q_{123}=0\) boundary.  It converts the two allowed singleton middle-cell areas into two minimum endpoint heights and charges their common overlap to the intervening doubleton endpoint cell.  Strict violation excludes a nonempty open parameter chamber.  The inequality does not, even together with the accepted crossing, tail, balance, convex three-cap, common-fan, and nine forced-cell capacity constraints, close the whole one-zero class: an exact rational scalar survivor is given and audited below.
author: mp_r399_midpoint_separator
proof:
Work in
\[
x=\theta_i,\qquad y=\theta_j,\qquad
\theta_k=-\sigma-x-y.
\tag{15}
\]
Let
\[
C_i=\overline{Q_i},\qquad C_k=\overline{Q_k}.
\]
Condition (3) supplies strict points in all five chambers used
below.  Segments from \(Q_i\) to \(Q_{ij}\) and \(Q_{ik}\) show,
respectively,
\[
\min_{C_i}y=0,\qquad
\max_{C_i}(x+y)=-\sigma.
\tag{16}
\]
Segments from \(Q_k\) to \(Q_{ik}\) and \(Q_{jk}\) give
\[
\min_{C_k}x=\min_{C_k}y=0.
\tag{17}
\]
Define
\[
a_i=\min_{C_i}x,\qquad
t_i=-\sigma-a_i,
\qquad
t_k=\max_{C_k}(x+y).
\tag{18}
\]
Then
\[
C_i\subseteq
\{x\geq a_i,\ y\geq0,\ x+y\leq-\sigma\},
\tag{19}
\]
\[
C_k\subseteq
\{x\geq0,\ y\geq0,\ x+y\leq t_k\}.
\tag{20}
\]

For any compact convex planar set \(C\), put
\[
t(C)=\max_C(x+y)-\min_Cx-\min_Cy.
\]
The exact Minkowski support identity used in
`9fdba5fffd591cda` is
\[
|T_\delta+C|_{\rm coord}
=\frac{\delta^2}{2}+|C|_{\rm coord}+\delta t(C).
\tag{21}
\]
It follows directly by expanding the ordered edge vectors, or by
adding the three support strips with outward normals
\((0,-1),(-1,0),(1,1)\).  Equations (16)--(20) say that
\(t(C_i)=t_i\) and \(t(C_k)=t_k\).

For \(s=i,k\), the two midpoint scores outside index \(s\) are
positive on \((P_0+Q_s)/2\).  Since the three middle scores sum to
\(-1\), the remaining score is negative.  Hence, up to null cutting
lines,
\[
\frac{\overline{P_0}+C_s}{2}\subseteq B\cap R_s.
\tag{22}
\]
Using (4), (21), and the area Jacobian in (22) gives
\[
\rho_s\geq
\frac14\left(p_0+q_s+\gamma\delta t_s\right).
\tag{23}
\]
Since \(\gamma\delta^2=2p_0\), equations (6) and (23) give
\[
\frac{t_s}{\delta}\leq R_s.
\tag{24}
\]

Let \(h_s\) be the maximum \(y\)-coordinate of \(C_s\), and
normalize
\[
\widehat t_s=\frac{t_s}{\delta},\qquad
\widehat h_s=\frac{h_s}{\delta}.
\]
At height \(y\), (19)--(20) bound the corresponding endpoint-cell
section length by \(t_s-y\).  Cavalieri integration therefore gives
\[
\frac{q_s}{2p_0}
=\frac{|C_s|_{\rm coord}}{\delta^2}
\leq
\widehat t_s\widehat h_s
-\frac{\widehat h_s^2}{2}
\leq
R_s\widehat h_s-\frac{\widehat h_s^2}{2}.
\tag{25}
\]
Here \(0<\widehat h_s\leq\widehat t_s\leq R_s\).
The right side of (25) is increasing on \([0,R_s]\).
It can reach \(q_s/(2p_0)\) only if (7) fails, and solving the
quadratic proves
\[
\widehat h_s\geq H_s.
\tag{26}
\]

For every
\[
0<y<\min\{h_i,h_k\},
\]
the horizontal section of \(A_2\) contains a \(C_i\)-point with
\(x\leq-\sigma-y\) and a \(C_k\)-point with \(x\geq0\).
Convexity forces the whole intervening interval
\[
[-\sigma-y,0],
\]
which is exactly the \(Q_{ik}\)-strip at that height.  Consequently
\[
\frac{q_{ik}}{\gamma}
\geq
\sigma h+\frac{h^2}{2},
\qquad
h=\min\{h_i,h_k\}.
\tag{27}
\]
Equations (26)--(27), together with
\(\gamma\delta^2=2p_0\) and
\(\sigma/\delta=\lambda\), prove (9).

Every inequality used above is an equality precisely under the
section-filling and no-excess conditions stated after (9).  This
proves the equality audit.  All radicals and inequalities depend
continuously on the positive parameters away from the equality
discriminants.  The exact strict separator in
`9fdba5fffd591cda` therefore proves the claimed nonempty open
exclusion chamber.

We finish by auditing (10)--(14).  Their four row totals are
\[
\sum_Jp_J=1,\qquad
\sum_Gq_G=\frac1{100},\qquad
\sum_G\rho_G=\frac{99}{100},\qquad
\sum_Gr_G=\frac{1981}{2000}.
\tag{28}
\]
The endpoint cap sums and endpoint-pair sums are
\[
(u_1,u_2,u_3)
=\left(\frac3{2000},\frac3{2000},\frac3{2000}\right),
\tag{29}
\]
\[
(v_1,v_2,v_3)
=\left(\frac{8499}{1000000},\frac7{2000},
\frac{2501}{1000000}\right),
\tag{30}
\]
\[
(d_1,d_2,d_3)
=\left(\frac{9999}{1000000},\frac1{200},
\frac{4001}{1000000}\right).
\tag{31}
\]
The middle cap sums are
\[
(b_1^0,b_2^0,b_3^0)
=\left(
\frac{3906509}{9000000},
\frac{7903}{18000},
\frac{3960491}{9000000}
\right),
\tag{32}
\]
\[
(b_1,b_2,b_3)
=\left(
\frac{3911009}{9000000},
\frac{989}{2250},
\frac{3964991}{9000000}
\right).
\tag{33}
\]
With
\[
\frac{2(M+m+k)}9=\frac{4001}{9000},
\]
direct addition gives
\[
d_s+b_s=\frac{4001}{9000}\qquad(s=1,2,3).
\tag{34}
\]
Moreover \(0<d_s<m\), so both canonical tails are strict.  Summing
the three crossings gives \(W=0\), equivalently
\[
3\left(\sum_su_s+\sum_sv_s+\sum_sb_s\right)
=2(M+m+k).
\tag{35}
\]
The balance inequalities are
\[
\frac{99}{100}<\frac{1981}{2000}<\frac{101}{100}.
\tag{36}
\]

For
\[
\mathcal R_X(c_1,c_2,c_3)
=5(c_1+c_2+c_3)-6\min_sc_s-4X,
\]
the four exact residuals are
\[
\mathcal R_M(M-u_1,M-u_2,M-u_3)
=\frac{9973}{2000},
\tag{37}
\]
\[
\mathcal R_m(v_1,v_2,v_3)
=\frac{8747}{500000},
\tag{38}
\]
\[
\mathcal R_{k_0}(b_1^0,b_2^0,b_3^0)
=\frac{747}{500000},
\qquad
\mathcal R_k(b_1,b_2,b_3)
=\frac{1997}{500000}.
\tag{39}
\]
Thus all four accepted convex three-cap constraints are strict.
Also
\[
k_0-
\left(\frac{3p_0+m}{4}+\frac{p_0}{\delta}\right)
=\frac{2801}{20000}>0,
\tag{40}
\]
and the ordinary total-area bound is weaker.

For a concise exact audit of all nine forced-cell capacities, put
\[
S(a,b,c)=\frac{4c-a-b}{2}.
\]
The inequality
\[
c>\frac14(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2
\]
follows exactly from \(S(a,b,c)>0\) and
\(S(a,b,c)^2-ab>0\).  In the order
\[
(p_0,q_1,\rho_1),\ (p_0,q_2,\rho_2),\
(p_0,q_3,\rho_3),
\]
\[
(p_1,q_1,\rho_1),\ (p_2,q_2,\rho_2),\
(p_3,q_3,\rho_3),
\]
\[
(p_{12},q_{12},\rho_{12}),\
(p_{13},q_{13},\rho_{13}),\
(p_{23},q_{23},\rho_{23}),
\]
the nine values of \(S\) are
\[
\frac{297409}{3600000},\ \frac{11}{720},\
\frac{62191}{3600000},\
\frac{2091109}{3600000},\ \frac{18487}{36000},\
\frac{1855891}{3600000},\
\frac1{1000},\ \frac3{2000},\ \frac{61}{750},
\tag{41}
\]
and the nine values of \(S^2-ab\) are
\[
\frac{10938314401}{12960000000000},\
\frac{121}{518400},\
\frac{3854799361}{12960000000000},
\]
\[
\frac{4372697976361}{12960000000000},\
\frac{341769169}{1296000000},\
\frac{3444331397401}{12960000000000},
\]
\[
\frac1{4000000},\ \frac1{500000},\
\frac{238117}{36000000}.
\tag{42}
\]
Every number in (41)--(42) is positive.

Finally we check the new separator without numerical radicals.
For \(s=3\), equations (6), (11)--(13) give
\[
R_3=\frac{62191}{3589200},\qquad
R_3^2-\frac{q_3}{p_0}
=\frac{3854799361}{12882356640000}>0.
\tag{43}
\]
At the rational normalized height \(z=1/30000\), one has
\(0<z<R_3\) and
\[
R_3z-\frac{z^2}{2}-\frac{q_3}{2p_0}
=\frac{406559}{5383800000000}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
Monotonicity in (25) shows \(H_3<z\), and hence \(H<z\).
Since \(\lambda=6/5\),
\[
q_{13}
-2p_0\left(\lambda z+\frac{z^2}{2}\right)
=\frac{378215003}{900000000000}>0.
\tag{45}
\]
Thus (9) also holds strictly.  Equations (28)--(45) prove that the
accepted scalar constraints plus the generalized separator have a
strict rational survivor.  Therefore (9) closes a nonempty open
parameter chamber but not the whole full-doubleton one-zero class at the
scalar level.
statement:
Let \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\).  Use the common-plane exact-cell
convention after accepted fact `8b9c428a36c45d68`.  Put
\[
\pi_s=f_s-L_s,\qquad \theta_s=f_s+L_s,
\]
\[
\delta=-1-(L_1+L_2+L_3)>0,\qquad
\sigma=\delta+2.
\tag{1}
\]
Let \(\gamma>0\) be the inverse area Jacobian of
\((\pi_i,\pi_j)\), equivalently of \((\theta_i,\theta_j)\).
Assume
\[
p_{ij}p_{ik}p_{jk}>0
\tag{2}
\]
and the full-doubleton one-zero singleton support conditions
\[
q_j=0,\qquad
q_iq_kq_{ij}q_{ik}q_{jk}>0.
\tag{3}
\]
Then accepted fact `cc8c0bf6093b9357` gives
\[
\overline{P_0}=T_\delta
:=\{(x,y):x\geq0,\ y\geq0,\ x+y\leq\delta\},
\qquad
p_0=\frac{\gamma\delta^2}{2}.
\tag{4}
\]

Let \(B\) be any compact convex body satisfying
\[
\frac{A_0+A_2}{2}\subseteq B,
\tag{5}
\]
and let \(\rho_G\) be its exact middle-cell areas.  For
\(s\in\{i,k\}\), define the dimensionless singleton allowance
\[
R_s=\frac{4\rho_s-p_0-q_s}{2p_0}.
\tag{6}
\]
If
\[
R_s<\sqrt{\frac{q_s}{p_0}}
\tag{7}
\]
for either \(s\), no such \(B\) exists.  Otherwise put
\[
H_s=R_s-\sqrt{R_s^2-\frac{q_s}{p_0}},
\qquad
H=\min\{H_i,H_k\},
\qquad
\lambda=\frac{\sigma}{\delta}=1+\frac2\delta.
\tag{8}
\]
Every realization necessarily satisfies the sharp midpoint
height-strip inequality
\[
\boxed{\qquad
q_{ik}\geq
2p_0\left(\lambda H+\frac{H^2}{2}\right).
\qquad}
\tag{9}
\]

The bounds entering (9) have the following equality
characterization.  Equality in the support bound defining \(R_s\)
requires the exact middle cell indexed by \(s\) to contain no
positive-area set outside
\((\overline{P_0}+\overline{Q_s})/2\).  Equality in the height
bound defining \(H_s\) requires \(\overline{Q_s}\), in the
normalized coordinates below, to fill its entire aligned triangle
truncated at that height.  Equality in (9) further requires the
\(Q_{ik}\)-section to be exactly the forced intervening strip on
the common vertical overlap and to have no positive-area part
outside that overlap.

Strict reverse inequality in (9) is an open exclusion condition.
The exact datum excluded by accepted fact `9fdba5fffd591cda`
lies strictly in this region, so the excluded parameter chamber is
nonempty.

The existing scalar constraints do not force this reverse
inequality.  Using the scalar conventions and gates certified in
accepted fact `38b9d85f6c0c57a2`, here is an exact rational
survivor.  Take
\[
(i,j,k)=(1,2,3),\qquad
M=1,\quad m=\frac1{100},\quad
k_0=\frac{99}{100},\quad k=\frac{1981}{2000},
\tag{10}
\]
\[
\delta=10,\qquad
\gamma=\frac{997}{50000},\qquad
p_0=\frac{997}{1000},
\tag{11}
\]
and put \(p_J=1/2000\) for every
\(J\in\{1,2,3,12,13,23\}\).  Set
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
G&1&2&3&12&13&23&123\\ \hline
q_G&
\frac{5999}{1000000}&0&\frac1{1000000}&
\frac3{2000}&\frac1{2000}&\frac3{2000}&\frac1{2000},
\end{array}
\tag{12}
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
G&1&2&3&12&13&23&123\\ \hline
\rho_G&
\frac{2628509}{9000000}&\frac{289}{1125}&
\frac{2320991}{9000000}&
\frac1{1000}&\frac1{1000}&\frac{247}{6000}&\frac7{50},
\end{array}
\tag{13}
\]
and let \(r_G=\rho_G\) except
\[
r_{123}=\frac{281}{2000}.
\tag{14}
\]
This table has all three crossings, both canonical tails strictly,
\(W=0\), and \(M-m<k<M+m\).  It passes strictly the four convex
three-cap tests for \(A_0,A_2,B,K\), the ordinary and common-fan
total-area gates, all nine forced single-cell capacities, and (9).
It is only a scalar calibration and makes no simultaneous planar
realizability claim.
